chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid — may God have mercy on him — reported to me from his father, from Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, saying:
God does not combine piety and renunciation of the world for a believer except that I have hope for him of Paradise. Then he said:

And indeed I love for the believing man among you, when he stands in his prayer, that he turns with his heart toward God the Exalted and does not let worldly affairs preoccupy him — for there is no believer who turns with his heart in his prayer toward God except that God turns toward him with His countenance, and turns the hearts of the believers toward him with love for him, after the love of God for him.
ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the reward for combining piety and renunciation with heart-presence in prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq teaches that combining piety (wara’) with renunciation of worldly attachments (zuhd) earns Paradise. He then emphasizes the importance of heart-presence (hudur al-qalb) during prayer: when a believer directs his heart fully toward God in prayer without worldly distractions, God reciprocates by turning His attention to the worshipper and filling the hearts of other believers with love for that person. This teaching was given to the Imam’s close companions in the context of spiritual counsel, where wara’ denotes scrupulous avoidance of the forbidden and zuhd refers to inner detachment from worldly allurements.
